messages:
alex: heads-up — noticed a perf regression when the paged/blocked KV cache starts fragmenting and the new fused-attn kernel falls back to scalar kernels. latency p95 spikes and GPU utilization drops. any ideas? :thinking:
maria: are we sure it's the kernel fallback and not just eviction thrash? can you paste the logs from the runtime selector?
alex: putting the selector trace below. you can see kernel_choice -> fused_attn failed compat check -> fallback_unoptimized. it correlates with lots of small page evicts.
```
selector: model_x_pruned_v2
sequence_len: 1024
kv_layout: fragmented(blocks=92, avg_block=14KB)
compat_check: contiguous_window=0 -> FAIL
selected_kernel: fallback_unoptimized
```

jordan: hmm, fused kernels require contiguous KV spans or at least a single stride mapping. fragmentation looks like the blocker. two possible angles: change kernel to accept scatter-gather or change cache to present a contiguous view. both have costs.
sam: changing kernel is tough; we lose perf on the common-case if we add SG support. i favor making the cache provide a logically contiguous handle with background compaction or pinning hot spans.
maria: agreed. maybe a small API between cache and kernel: cache.export_contiguous_handle(start, len) that either returns a direct pointer or a trivial shim that assembles pages into a bounce buffer. kernel then uses handle->type to pick optimized path. this keeps kernel selection local.
alex: yeah — that handshake would make runtime selector simpler: it just asks cache for contiguous_handle and checks handle.type == DIRECT to pick fused. otherwise fallback. but we need to consider GC/eviction semantics. pinning pages to keep DIRECT has memory tax.
jordan: tradeoffs: pinning hot spans reduces eviction but increases peak memory. compaction reduces fragmentation but can be CPU-heavy and induce jitter. bounce-buffering copies data per-request which hurts throughput. need telemetry budget to decide.
sam: propose heuristic: if request window <= 64k and cache reports >90% DIRECT availability => use fused kernel. else use fallback. also introduce a "pin_hint" that increments a hot-counter for a span, and background compactor tries to coalesce spans with hot-counter > threshold.
maria: can we make compaction incremental and IO-friendly? e.g., move only the least fragmented neighbor pages per cycle and respect SLOs. also add a metric: contiguous_bytes_ratio per-model and per-route.
alex: i sketched an API change in runtime-config. thoughts?
```
{
  "kernel_hint": "needs_contiguous",
  "cache_api": {
    "export_handle(start, len)": "returns {type: DIRECT|BOUNCE|COMPACT_PENDING, ptr_or_token}" 
  },
  "pin_hint": "optional bool",
  "contig_threshold_bytes": 65536
}
```

jordan: looks reasonable. we should also expose a compatibility-level in the model catalog metadata (e.g., contig_preferred: true/false) so selector can prefer older kernels for models that are naturally fragmented (pruned, fused).
sam: testing plan: reproduce with synthetic workload that writes KV at 16KB page granularity and runs seq_len 1024 generations for 30m. measure p95, fused_kernel_success_rate, compaction_cpu. add a canary rollout gating on fused_kernel_success_rate >= 0.85.
maria: operational concerns: add alerts for compaction backlog and pinned_memory_ratio > 0.15. also a dashboard heatmap for fragmentation over time.
ci-bot: perf-test/job-879 started: blocked-cache-frag-sim, ETA ~18m. will post results.
alex: thanks. followups: 1) i'll prototype the export_handle shim. 2) sam+jord will define compaction policy and counters. 3) maria will add metrics to runtime telemetry. aim for initial patch next week. :thumbsup:
maria: +1. can we also add a small synthetic that simulates model pruning fragmentation? helps validate heuristics.
sam: yep, i'll add that to job-879 if CI-bot allows.
jordan: if compaction looks too heavy we can fall back to a mempool for hot spans (pre-allocated contiguous buffer) and stream non-hot to bounce path. that keeps tail predictable.
alex: good idea. ok team — let's iterate. will post prototype thread when I have export_handle PoC. :rocket:
